s: Holiness is victoriously maintained by king Vîstâspa against the host of the fiends. The friends of Astvat-ereta follow the good law, and Holiness is called the best of all good.

l: Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XX. Vanant Yast.
s: The unit is the XX. Vanant Yast, concerning worship, sacrifice, and prayer to the star Vanant, made by Ahura Mazda. The worshipper identifies himself as a worshipper of Mazda, a follower of Zarathustra, one who hates the Daêvas, and an observer of Ahura’s laws. Vanant is invoked as strong and healing to withstand the accursed Khrafstras of Angra Mainyu. The unit asks for brightness, glory, and a blissful abode for a man.

l: XX. Vanant Yast, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XX. Vanant Yast.
s: The XX. Vanant Yast concerns sacrifice, prayer, propitiation, and glorification directed to the star Vanant.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XX. Vanant Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda is named as the maker of Vanant. His laws are obeyed by the worshipper, who identifies himself as a worshipper of Mazda.

l: Daêvas, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XX. Vanant Yast.
s: The worshipper identifies himself as one who hates the Daêvas.

l: Vanant, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XX. Vanant Yast.
s: Vanant is described as a star made by Mazda, holy and master of holiness. Sacrifice and prayer are offered to Vanant, who is invoked as strong and healing to withstand the accursed Khrafstras of Angra Mainyu.

l: Angra Mainyu, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XX. Vanant Yast.
s: Angra Mainyu is described as most abominable, and the Khrafstras are identified as his accursed and most foul creatures.

l: Khrafstras, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XX. Vanant Yast.
s: The Khrafstras are described as accursed and most foul, and Vanant is invoked to withstand them.

l: Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXI. Yast Fragment.
s: Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda which word contains the glorification of all good things made by the good principle. Ahura Mazda answers that it is the praise of Holiness, which praises him, the waters, the earth, the cattle, the plants, and all good things made by Mazda. He explains that its value increases when recited during specific acts and times, especially with professions of good thoughts, words, and deeds and rejection of evil ones. The final recital, made to renounce evil thoughts, words, and deeds, is said to equal all that lies between earth and the heavens, the earth, luminous space, and all good things made by Mazda.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXI. Yast Fragment.
s: Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda about the word containing the glorification of all good things and about the recitals of the praise of Holiness. He is addressed as Spitama Zarathustra and as holy Zarathustra.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXI. Yast Fragment.
s: Ahura Mazda answers Zarathustra that the word is the praise of Holiness. He teaches that its recitation praises him and all good things made by Mazda, and he describes the circumstances in which its value is increased.

l: praise of Holiness, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXI. Yast Fragment.
s: The praise of Holiness glorifies Ahura Mazda, the waters, the earth, the cattle, the plants, and all good things that are the offspring of the good principle. Its recitation is assigned increasing value when performed while eating, drinking Haoma, waking, sleeping, rising, dying, or renouncing evil thoughts, words, and deeds.

l: Holiness, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXI. Yast Fragment.
s: Holiness is praised through a recital that also praises Ahura Mazda and the good things made by Mazda. Beings of Holiness are mentioned in comparison with the value of this recital.

l: the Good Principle, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXI. Yast Fragment.
s: The good principle is the source of the good things made by Mazda. The praise of Holiness glorifies those things as its offspring.

l: Ahuna Vairya, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXI. Yast Fragment.
s: Ahuna Vairya is identified as the formula whose pronouncing, together with the reciting of the word of truth, increases strength and victory in one's soul and piety.

l: Karshvare Hvaniratha, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXI. Yast Fragment.
s: Karshvare Hvaniratha is described as this Karshvare, with its cattle and chariots but without its men. One recital of the praise of Holiness, delivered in the last moments of life while professing good thoughts, words, and deeds and rejecting evil ones, is said to equal it in greatness, goodness, and fairness.

l: Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: Yast XXII concerns Zarathustra’s questions to Ahura Mazda about the souls of the faithful and the wicked after death. The faithful person’s soul remains near the head for three nights, then encounters its conscience and enters successive paradises, ending in the Endless Lights. The wicked person’s soul remains near the skull for three nights, then enters successive hells, ending in the Endless Darkness. The unit also describes the food of the departed, the manifestation of holy souls, and the lying call of Bûshyãsta.

l: Yast XXII, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: Yast XXII describes the postmortem experiences of faithful and wicked people, their souls’ destinations, and related teachings from Ahura Mazda.
Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda where the souls of faithful and wicked people abide after death and what they experience.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: Ahura Mazda explains the three-night experiences, destinations, and nourishment of the souls of faithful and wicked people. He also says that the souls and Fravashis of the holy Ones manifest through goodness of spirit and excellence of mind.

l: faithful person, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: The faithful person has good thoughts, good words, good deeds, and good religion. After death, the faithful person’s conscience appears as a beautiful maiden reflecting those qualities.

For three nights, the faithful person’s soul sits near the head, sings the Ustavaiti Gâtha, and tastes pleasure. At the third-night dawn it encounters a sweet-scented wind and its own conscience, then enters the Good-Thought Paradise, Good-Word Paradise, Good-Deed Paradise, and Endless Lights.

The faithful person’s conscience appears at the third-night dawn as a beautiful maiden and explains that the person’s good thoughts, words, and deeds made her more lovely, fair, desirable, and honored.

l: wicked person, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: The wicked person has evil thoughts, evil words, evil deeds, and evil religion. After death, the wicked person receives poison and poisonous stench as food.

l: wicked person's soul, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: For three nights, the wicked person’s soul rushes and sits near the skull, singing the Kima Gâtha and tasting suffering. At the third-night dawn it encounters snow, stench, and a foul-scented northern wind, then enters the Evil-Thought Hell, Evil-Word Hell, Evil-Deed Hell, and Endless Darkness.

l: Angra Mainyu, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: Angra Mainyu, described as the lying one, says not to question the wicked person who has just traveled the dreary way between body and soul.

l: material world, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: The material world is described as an abode full of cattle, wishes, and enjoyments of love, and as a decaying world contrasted with the world of the spirit.

l: world of the spirit, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: The world of the spirit is contrasted with the material world and is described as undecaying.

l: Good-Thought Paradise, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: The Good-Thought Paradise is where the faithful person’s soul arrives after its first step.

l: Good-Word Paradise, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: The Good-Word Paradise is where the faithful person’s soul arrives after its second step.

l: Good-Deed Paradise, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: The Good-Deed Paradise is where the faithful person’s soul arrives after its third step.

l: Endless Lights, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: The Endless Lights are where the faithful person’s soul arrives after its fourth step.

l: Evil-Thought Hell, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: The Evil-Thought Hell is where the wicked person’s soul is laid after its first step.

l: Evil-Word Hell, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: The Evil-Word Hell is where the wicked person’s soul is laid after its second step.

l: Evil-Deed Hell, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: The Evil-Deed Hell is where the wicked person’s soul is laid after its third step.

l: Endless Darkness, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: The Endless Darkness is where the wicked person’s soul is laid after its fourth step.

l: faithful person's death, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: After the faithful person’s death, the soul remains near the head for three nights, then travels through paradises to the Endless Lights.

l: wicked person's death, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: After the wicked person’s death, the soul remains near the skull for three nights, then travels through hells to the Endless Darkness.

l: third-night dawn, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: At the third-night dawn, the faithful person’s soul experiences plants, scents, and a sweet-scented southern wind, while the wicked person’s soul experiences snow, stench, and a foul-scented northern wind.

l: third night, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: On the third night, the faithful person’s soul remains near the head in pleasure, while the wicked person’s soul remains near the skull in suffering.

l: good thoughts, good words, and good deeds, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: Good thoughts, good words, and good deeds characterize the faithful person and determine the successive paradises reached by the faithful person’s soul.

l: evil thoughts, evil words, and evil deeds, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yast XXII.
s: Evil thoughts, evil words, and evil deeds characterize the wicked person and determine the successive hells reached by the wicked person’s soul.

l: Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Âfrîn Paighambar Zartûst / XXIII. Âfrîn Paighambar Zartûst.
s: Âfrîn Paighambar Zartûst presents Zarathustra blessing king Vîstâspa. He wishes Vîstâspa a long, exalted, good life, long-lived people and women, sons, strength, glory, wealth, holiness, victory, welfare, and freedom from sickness and death. He names models for these qualities, including Gâmâspa, Mazda, Thraêtaona, Yima Khshaêta, and Zarathustra Spitama. The blessing concludes by calling for the propagation of good thoughts, good words, and good deeds and for entry into the bright abode of the holy Ones.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Âfrîn Paighambar Zartûst / XXIII. Âfrîn Paighambar Zartûst.
s: Âfrîn Paighambar Zartûst presents Zarathustra speaking a blessing to king Vîstâspa. The blessing invokes a good, exalted, and long life, many virtues, sons, welfare, victory, and freedom from sickness and death.

l: Vîstâspa, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Âfrîn Paighambar Zartûst / XXIII. Âfrîn Paighambar Zartûst.
s: King Vîstâspa receives Zarathustra’s blessing as lord of the country. He is wished long life, long-lived men and women, sons, beneficence, strength, glory, wealth, holiness, victory, welfare, and freedom from sickness and death.

l: blessing, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Âfrîn Paighambar Zartûst / XXIII. Âfrîn Paighambar Zartûst.
s: The blessing wishes Vîstâspa to resemble various exemplary figures in beneficence, fiend-smiting, strength, arms, glory, instruction, might, leadership, beauty, wealth, holiness, speed, radiance, heat, piercing rays, truth, conquest, welfare, and freedom from sickness and death. It concludes with a wish that the blessing come true and lead to the bright, all-happy, blissful abode of the holy Ones.

l: Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: The unit concerns Zarathustra's teachings and blessings for the young king Vîstâspa, including prosperity, holiness, long life, strength, offspring, and royal power. It describes the Law of the worshippers of Mazda, proper priests and sacrifices, prayers, moral conduct, charity, and the defeat of evil. It teaches that the faithful soul reaches Garô-nmâna through Good Thoughts, Good Words, Good Deeds, and Endless Light, meeting its own conscience along the way. Ahura Mazda and the Amesha-Spentas are presented as granting glory, protection, guidance, and the rewards of holiness.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: Zarathustra blesses and teaches the young king Vîstâspa, instructing him in holiness, the Law of the worshippers of Mazda, proper sacrifice, prayer, charity, and the defeat of evil. He teaches how the faithful soul reaches Garô-nmâna and addresses Ahura Mazda with worship.

l: Vîstâspa, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: Vîstâspa is blessed with holiness, long life, prosperity, offspring, strength, glory, swift horses, and royal power. He is taught to support the Law of the worshippers of Mazda, reject bad or unfriendly priests, perform proper sacrifices, pray, help the poor, and follow the right way.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda is invoked as the Maker of the good world and as full of Glory. He grants guidance, protection, glory, healing, prosperity, and the heavenly reward, and explains the soul's journey after death.

l: Amesha-Spentas, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: The Amesha-Spentas are invoked to grant greatness, brightness, glory, plenty, protection, and guidance. They promise to show Zarathustra the way to the spiritual world and Paradise.

l: good Law of the worshippers of Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: The Law is presented as holy, victorious, protective, and life-giving. It should be supported, proclaimed, practiced, embraced, and given even to those who are unfriendly, while its followers should care for the poor and avoid evil conduct.

l: Ashem Vohû, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: Holiness is described as the best of all good. It brings prosperity, protection, knowledge, spiritual progress, and passage over the Kinvat-bridge to the blessed abodes.

l: Angra Mainyu, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: Angra Mainyu is the Evil Spirit, and his influence is to be kept away. His evil is associated with lust, derision, idolatry, rejection of the poor, and other harmful acts.

l: Garô-nmâna, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: Garô-nmâna is the beautifully made and fully adorned abode of Ahura Mazda. The faithful reach it through the stages of Good Thoughts, Good Words, Good Deeds, and Endless Light.

l: Kinvat-bridge, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: The Kinvat-bridge is a powerful, well-kept bridge known afar and kept by virtue. The soul of man crosses it in the joy of perfect holiness.

l: soul, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: The faithful soul separates from the body and spends the first night in Good Words and the second in Good Deeds before going along the ways to Garô-nmâna. It encounters its own conscience and reaches the Good-Thought, Good-Word, Good-Deed, and Endless Light Paradises.

l: conscience, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: The conscience of the faithful appears as a beautiful maiden and identifies herself as the person's own conscience. She reflects the person's good thoughts, words, deeds, religion, and treatment of the faithful and the poor.

l: Âtar, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: Fire, the son of Ahura Mazda, is worshipped as a valiant warrior. It falls upon Kunda, the men of the Drug, the slothful ones, and the wicked Daêva-worshippers, and its perfume drives them away.

l: Ashem Vohû, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: Ashem Vohû is repeatedly proclaimed with the teaching that holiness is the best of all good. It is spoken in blessings, invocations, and ritual instruction.

l: faithful person, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: The faithful man supports the Law, performs proper worship and sacrifice, helps the poor, and follows good thoughts, words, deeds, and religion. After death, he receives a sweet-scented wind, encounters his conscience, and proceeds through the Paradises to Endless Light.

l: priest, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: A priest should be treated like the brightest offspring of one's own blood and should not be bad or unfriendly. A sacrifice offered through bad or unfriendly priests is treated as though no sacrifice had been offered to the Amesha-Spentas.

l: worshippers of Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: The worshippers of Mazda follow the Law, practice holiness, perform sacrifices and prayers, and walk in its ways. Their Law is connected with protection, prosperity, spiritual knowledge, and the defeat of the Drug.

l: sacrifice, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: A sacrifice to Ahura Mazda's creation must be performed according to the rites, including the use of baresma and Haoma. Proper sacrifice brings royalty and helps protect and advance the worshipper.

l: Good-Word Paradise, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIV. Vîstâsp Yast.
s: Paradise is reached by the faithful soul after death through Good Thoughts, Good Words, and Good Deeds. The text names the Good-Thought, Good-Word, and Good-Deed Paradises, followed by Endless Light and the Garô-nmâna of Ahura Mazda.

l: Nyayish, Nyayish, Nyayish / I. Khôrshêd Nyâyis.
s: This unit is a hymn to the Sun, Ahura Mazda, and other holy beings. It praises good thoughts, words, and deeds, rejects evil ones, and offers sacrifice and prayer to the Amesha-Spentas and other sacred entities. It invokes Mithra, Tistrya, the Sun, and Ahura Mazda for help, health, glory, and a blessed abode. It also includes repeated recitations of Ashem Vohû and identifies the worshipper as a follower of Zarathustra.

l: Ahura Mazda, Nyayish, Nyayish / I. Khôrshêd Nyâyis.
s: Ahura Mazda is hailed before all other creatures and is asked to be rejoiced. He is invoked with the Amesha-Spentas, Mithra, and the Sun, and is described as having the Sun as two eyes.

l: Sun, Nyayish, Nyayish / I. Khôrshêd Nyâyis.
s: The Sun is hailed as swift-horsed, bright, undying, and shining. Sacrifices are offered to it, and it is honored as being in accord with the Amesha-Spentas and as one of the two eyes of Ahura Mazda.

l: Amesha-Spentas, Nyayish, Nyayish / I. Khôrshêd Nyâyis.
s: The Amesha-Spentas are hailed as being of one accord with the Sun. Prayers, sacrifice, and the worshipper’s thoughts, words, deeds, heart, and life are offered to them.

l: Ashem Vohû, Nyayish, Nyayish / I. Khôrshêd Nyâyis.
s: Ashem Vohû is recited as a praise of holiness. It teaches that holiness is the best of all good and that holiness is associated with perfection.

l: Mithra, Nyayish, Nyayish / I. Khôrshêd Nyâyis.
s: Mithra is hailed as the lord of wide pastures and is described as truth-speaking, a chief in assemblies, well-shaped, strong, sleepless, and ever awake. He is invoked together with Ahura Mazda for help, and sacrifices are offered to him.

l: Spitama Zarathustra, Nyayish, Nyayish / I. Khôrshêd Nyâyis.
s: The Fravashi of the holy Spitama Zarathustra is hailed. The worshipper identifies himself as a follower of Zarathustra.

l: Tistrya, Nyayish, Nyayish / I. Khôrshêd Nyâyis.
s: Tistrya is honored as a bright and glorious star whose sight is sound. Sacrifices are offered to Tistrya and to his rains.

This unit is a prayer and liturgical offering to Ahura Mazda, the Amesha-Spentas, Mithra, and other holy beings. It asks that the prayer reach Ahura Mazda, the Amesha-Spentas, the Fravashis of the holy Ones, and Vayu. It praises good thoughts, words, and deeds, and seeks health, holiness, brightness, and glory. Much of the unit concerns sacrifice and prayer to Mithra, who is described as powerful, watchful, truth-speaking, and lord of wide pastures and all countries.

l: Ahura Mazda, Nyayish, II. Mihir Nyâyis.
s: Ahura Mazda is hailed before all other creatures and asked to receive the prayer. He is said to have made Mithra the most glorious of all the heavenly gods, and the worshipper asks that Ahura Mazda be rejoiced.
The Amesha-Spentas are hailed as being of one accord with the Sun. The prayer is asked to come to them, and sacrifices and prayers are offered to them.

The prayer is directed to Ahura Mazda, the Amesha-Spentas, the Fravashis of the holy Ones, and Vayu. It praises good thoughts, words, and deeds and seeks health, holiness, brightness, glory, and a blissful abode.

Sacrifice is offered to the Amesha-Spentas, Mithra, Ahura Mazda, the Sun, Tistrya, the holy gods, the stars, the moon, and other sacred beings. Libations are offered to Mithra, and the strength and vigour of Mithra are blessed.
The world is described as eventually coming to an end. The unit asks for the highest luminous space when that occurs and refers to holy gods of the world unseen.

Mithra is described as the lord of wide pastures and all countries, truth-speaking, powerful, watchful, sleepless, and ever awake. Sacrifices and libations are offered to him, and he is invoked with Ahura as a great and imperishable holy god for help and ease.

This unit is a series of praises, sacrifices, and prayers concerning Ahura Mazda and the Moon that keeps in it the seed of the Bull. It also concerns the Amesha-Spentas, the Bull, the gods of full Glory and healing, and the Waters. The speaker asks for strength, victory, welfare, abundant male children, and blessings of brightness, glory, and a blissful abode for those who offer sacrifice.

l: Ahura Mazda, Nyayish, III. Mâh Nyâyis.
s: Ahura Mazda is hailed, and the unit opens with a salutation to him. The speaker also recites the Yathâ aha vairyô, describing the will of the Lord as the law of holiness.

The Moon is described as keeping in it the seed of the Bull and is associated with the only-created Bull and the Bull of many species. It is hailed, observed as it looks upon those who look at it, asked about as it waxes and wanes, and worshipped through sacrifices for its brightness and glory.

This unit concerns Ahura Mazda’s praise and worship of the good waters and the holy water-spring Ardvi Sûra Anâhita. Ahura Mazda tells Spitama Zarathustra to offer sacrifices to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita, who purifies male seed and female wombs and whose river supplies waters across the seven Karshvares. The text describes offerings made to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita with libations, Haoma, meat, baresma, holy spells, words, deeds, and rightly-spoken words. It asks for brightness, glory, and a blissful abode for the man who worships properly.

l: Ahura Mazda, Nyayish, IV. Âbân Nyâyis.
s: Ahura Mazda is praised as the maker of the good waters and plants and speaks to Spitama Zarathustra. He tells Spitama Zarathustra to sacrifice to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita and says that he brought her river down for the increase of houses, boroughs, towns, and countries.

l: Spitama Zarathustra, Nyayish, IV. Âbân Nyâyis.
s: Spitama Zarathustra is addressed by Ahura Mazda and instructed to offer a sacrifice to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita. He is told to advise others when appealed to and to worship her fully.

l: Ardvi Sûra Anâhita, Nyayish, IV. Âbân Nyâyis.
s: Ardvi Sûra Anâhita is described as a holy water-spring and a large river whose waters spread across the seven Karshvares. She purifies the seed of males and the wombs of females, and she grants requested boons to the man who hears and performs the holy words and makes the good waters pure.

This unit concerns prayers and offerings to Ahura Mazda and Âtar, the son of Ahura Mazda. Âtar is praised as beneficent, powerful, healing, and worthy of sacrifice and invocation. Worshippers ask Âtar for welfare, knowledge, courage, offspring, prosperity, and a place among the holy Ones. Âtar blesses those who bring him properly prepared sacred wood and other offerings, while he watches what passers-by bring.

l: Ahura Mazda, Nyayish, V. Âtas Nyâyis
s: Ahura Mazda is addressed as the source of Âtar and as the deity whose glory, beneficence, and works are praised. The worshipper asks Ahura Mazda for perfect piety and strength and gladdens his mighty, quick, and powerful Fire.

l: Âtar, the son of Ahura Mazda, Nyayish, V. Âtas Nyâyis
s: Âtar, the son of Ahura Mazda, receives sacrifice, prayer, propitiation, glorification, sacred wood, incense, food, fuel, and other offerings. He is described as beneficent, a warrior, a full source of glory and healing, and as dwelling with all Âtars alongside Nairyô-sangha in the navel of kings. He watches what passers-by bring and blesses those who offer properly prepared wood, granting them growing herds, sons, mastery of their vows, and joy of soul.

Yasna I–XXVII is a connected cycle of Mazdayasnian ritual worship, sacrifice, confession, offerings, and sacred commentary centered on Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Righteousness, the Fire, Haoma, the waters, plants, Fravashis, and the many Yazads. The speaker repeatedly declares allegiance to Mazda-worship and Zarathustra’s order, rejects the Daêvas and wicked powers, confesses possible failures of thought, word, and deed, and seeks to complete the Yasna rightly. The early units establish the ritual: approaching the Zaothra and Baresman; offering Haoma, Myazda, milk, water, wood, plants, meat, and prayers; honoring ritual lords, sacred times and places, and priestly authority shared by the Zaotar and Ratu. The rites are presented as benefiting homes, herds, people, descendants, settlements, and the righteous. They include blessings, protection, prosperity, health, victory, wisdom, and the repression of the wicked. Yasna IX–XI focus on H(a)oma: its revelation to Zarathustra, its preparers Vîvanghvant, Âthwya, Thrita, and Pourushaspa, its association with Yima, Thraêtaona, Keresâspa, and Zarathustra, and its powers of healing, victory, protection, and sacred exhilaration. Yasna XII gives the Mazdayasnian Confession, explicitly rejecting the Daêvas and affirming Mazda, Asha, the Kine, sacred creation, Zarathustra’s creed, and future Saoshyants. Later units continue dedications to Ahura Mazda, Zarathustra, the Faith, Fire, waters, mountains, sacred words, and the Fravashis of saints, including the dead, living, unborn, teachers, and children. Yasna XVIII petitions Mazda for Immortality, Weal, and Spirit bounteous. Yasna XIX–XXI shift into commentary on the Ahuna-vairya, Ashem Vohû, and Yênhê Hâtãm, explaining their righteousness, salvation, structure, recitation, and sacrificial use. The collection closes by renewing ritual offerings and honoring Fravashis, then affirming Ahura Mazda’s kingdom and the sacred power of the Ahuna-vairya and Asha Vahista against Angra Mainyu, Aêshma, and wicked Daêvas.

The Yasna is a sacrifice and sacrificial worship of Mazda. It is announced and completed with confession and increased praise, continues by naming worshipped beings, sacred things, places, times, and observances, and is offered by the worshipper to the Bountiful Immortals and holy beings.

Ahura Mazda is the Creator: radiant, glorious, greatest, best, wisest, holy, and most beneficent. He made the speaker and the good creation, including the corporeal worlds, creatures, Fire, waters, plants, the Kine, mountains, the Wind, and the dwelling-place. Fire is called his son, while the waters and other sacred things are Mazda-made. He fashions, nourishes, protects, and provides nurture, especially for the poor; he rules the Kingdom and is asked to reign with a saving rule over his creatures. He is the central recipient of worship: sacrifice, homage, propitiation, praise, prayers, gifts, offerings, and confessions of debt are directed to him. Ritual offerings and sacred objects are presented to him, and he is associated with H(a)oma through the girdle he bears, the portions he chooses, and the offering he gives to bless H(a)oma. He is also the holy lord of the ritual order and the source or speaker of sacred words, including Ashem Vohû and the Ahuna-vairya. The records portray him as prior to the whole creation and supreme over it: he thought, spoke, disposed, and did all things good; recognizes sanctity and superior fidelity; repels the evil one; and grants salvation. He tells Zarathustra that Ahuna-vairya preceded sky, waters, land, creatures, and the corporeal world, and that its proper recitation can bring a soul to Heaven. His holy Fravashi is worshipped as greatest and best, attaining its ends through Righteousness.

Righteousness the Best is a Bountiful Immortal, religious principle, and the best ritual order, also identified as Asha Vahista. It governs thought, word, and deed, stands before all other things in the holy man’s thought, and supports homage to the good Yazads. Across the Yasna, it is announced, celebrated, praised, approached, offered to, and worshipped alongside holy lords of ritual order and Ahura Mazda’s Fire. It is linked with Rapithwina, named among the Lords of Asha, and called the best or most beautiful Bountiful Immortal. It is also the principle for which the Ahuna-vairya is learned and recited; creatures that place it first perform the deed well done. The sequence closes by invoking and worshipping it as the most beautiful Bountiful Immortal.
Ameretatât is a Bountiful Immortal identified with Immortality, guarding plants and wood; it is offered meat and flesh for propitiation, while Immortality is requested from Mazda.

Kine are sacred, blessed gifts associated with food and pasture, belonging to Ahura Mazda and linked with Asha and religious sanctity. Their flesh is offered in propitiation and sacrifice. The speaker rejects robbery and violence against them and seeks to remove their wandering as they abide steadfastly on land.
Kine's Soul, belonging to saints, is worshipped with holy souls of the dead, living, and unborn, and finds satisfaction and delight in works of Righteousness.

Fire of Ahura Mazda is a fire and son of Ahura Mazda, the lofty lord of the entire holy creation and lord of the friendly and most helpful person. It is announced and celebrated with all fires as a recipient of the Yasna, then receives offerings for sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise. Its perfume is presented, and its lofty lordship is affirmed.

Hâvani is both a holy lord of the ritual order and a ritual time. It receives sacrifice, homage, propitiation, praise, and requests for forgiveness. At Hâvani, the Baresman and Zaothra are brought to their appointed place, and ritual lords are approached. Thirty and three lords are arranged nearest around it; its services were inculcated by Mazda and pronounced by Zarathustra.

Mithra is a Yazad of the spoken name, repeatedly portrayed as lofty, everlasting or imperishable, holy, wide-pastured, thousand-eared, and myriad-eyed. He governs or is lord of all the provinces and is associated with Raman Hvâstra. Across Yasna I, Mithra is announced and celebrated as province-ruler. Yasna II approaches him with praise in the Zaothra and Baresman. Yasna III names him alongside Ahura as one of the lofty and imperishable two and as province-lord. Yasna VI worships him both in his own attributes and with Ahura as one of the lofty, imperishable, holy two. Yasna VII reiterates these qualities, his connection with Ahura, and his lordship of the provinces.

Waters are Mazda-made, holy, good, beneficial natural entities. They are worshipped as the good and best waters, receive offerings including Haoma, Haoma-water, milk, Hadhânaêpata, Zaothras, the stone, and the iron mortar, and are included among sacred things. They figure in instruction for Mazdayasnians and are among sacred beings over which the holy man has sovereignty.

The Fravashis of the saints are good, heroic, bountiful, holy, redoubted, mighty, and overwhelming. They belong to the saints and provide mighty, overwhelming succour for them. Across the Yasna, they are announced and celebrated, approached with Yasts, praise, and worship, and repeatedly receive offerings for sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise. They are associated with ancient lore, next of kin, pious women, girls, maidens diligent among the cattle, and saints both dead and living. Worship includes them with the stars, moon, sun, Ahura, and Mithra, and specifically includes the sacred Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma. They are also named with Ahura Mazda as those who name the month.

Sraosha is a blessed Yazad identified with Obedience. He is good, holy, stately, mighty, and endowed with sanctity; Mãthra is his body. His central action is to smite or strike with victory, especially the blow of victory, thereby furthering or causing settlements to advance. Across the records, he is repeatedly propitiated and worshipped through sacrifice, a Yast, meat offerings, sacred flesh, and the flesh of the Kine of blessed gift. He is also a holy lord of the ritual order and has a daring spear. The descriptions move from his identity and victorious power to repeated ritual offerings and worship.

l: three and thirty lords of the ritual order, Yasna
s: The three and thirty Lords of Asha Vahishta approach nearest at Hâvani; Mazda inculcated and Zarathustra pronounced their services as feasts of Righteousness, the Best.
Spenta Mainyu creates stars and has creatures through which wickedness is carried out; holy male and female creatures receive the Yasna.
Moon, a holy lord of ritual order in new, waning, and full forms, is approached with Baresman in worship and contains seeds of Kine and cattle in its beams.
The Sun is resplendent and fleet-horsed, the eye of Ahura Mazda, and receives an offering with Ahura and Mithra.

l: Fravashis of the saints (ancient lore), Yasna
s: The Fravashis of the saints are good, heroic, and bountiful spiritual beings of ancient lore. Existing from of old, they encompass those of houses, villages, communities, provinces, the house, Vîs, Zantuma, Dahvyuma, Zarathustrôtema, Ahura Mazda, and holy persons. They hold heaven, water, land, and cattle apart, and protect children in the womb from miscarriage. They are associated with saints and their next-of-kin, and are praised, invoked, glorified, and worshipped with good Yasnas and homage. The records proceed from their identity and scope, through their protective ordering of the world, to honor for holy teachers, disciples, children, men, and women from Gaya Maretan to Saoshyant.

Zarathustrian law is a holy, bounteous, effective Mazdayasnian revelation and Mãthra Spenta, pronounced and instituted against the Daêvas. It matters as a glorious sacred law and bounteous word of reason, imparting heart’s devotion to the saint. It is first named among sacred objects receiving a complete offering, then worshipped and identified with Mãthra, science, and Mazda-made understanding.

is_a revelation [given against the Daêvas] The Zarathustrian revelation is described as the Bounteous Mãthra, holy and effective, and as a revelation given against the Daêvas. It is announced and completed in the Yasna.

The Mazdayasnian Faith is a good religion with a long descent, announced and completed in the Yasna. It is worshipped and named with Mãthra Spenta and the Zarathustrian law, then identified with the good Religion. As Mazdayasnian law, it is addressed alongside the Bountiful Immortals, just men and women, and Zaothras, and connected to teaching liberality of Righteousness. Praised as holy, imposing, best, and most beautiful, it includes kindred marriage, has no faltering utterance, and wields the felling halbert. Blessed and good, it is invoked with its sciences, forces, fire-priests, charioteers, warriors, and tillers. Its blessings accompany sacrifice; its fulfilment, Gâtha recital, and propitiation belong to ritual. Finally, recollection and practice are offerings, and its law is worshipped as most true, Mazda-made, holy religious Knowledge.
Mount Ushi-darena is a Mazda-made mountain and Yazad mount, glorious and shining with holiness, worshipped in Yasna XVII.
Mountains are Mazda-made, holy, glorious places of ritual order, shining with holiness and abundant glory, where H(a)oma grows and birds carry it across peaks, gorges, abysses, and snowy summits.

Earth is wide, holy, productive, and full bearing: bounteous Âramaiti, bearing us and serving as home to healthy herds, healthy men, and persons. Addressed as the dwelling-place and abode of Ahura Mazda, it receives a plea for helpful, preserving influences through summer and winter.
Sacred creatures of Spenta Mainyu, the stars are approached with Baresman in worship and receive offerings.

l: holy creatures of the Spenta Mainyu, Yasna
s: Holy creatures of the Spenta Mainyu, male and female regulators of ritual order, are included among those to whom offerings are announced and presented.

The three and thirty lords are holy chieftains and lords of the ritual order, lords of Righteousness the Best. They are worthy of sacrifice and come nearest round about the Hâvanis at Hâvani. Ahura Mazda instituted their observances, and Zarathustra spoke them forth. Within the ritual order, they are announced and approached with praise, sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and worship; the speaker also seeks forgiveness for offenses against them.

The Yazads are holy, beneficent heavenly and earthly beings who dispose all things aright; the Yasna presents them as fit for sacrifice and homage, praising, invoking, and glorifying them, including Nairya-sangha.

Daêvas are evil, deceitful, wicked beings, bereft of good and most like the Demon-of-the-Lie. They are foes of Mazda-worshippers and the Mazdayasnian confession, and the Zarathustrian law is composed against them. Zarathustra seeks H(a)oma’s protection against their hate. They are finally driven away and wholly abjured, including their shelter, headship, thoughts, words, actions, seed, sorcerers, adherents, and associates.

Zarathustra, also called Zarathustra Spitâma, is a saint, holy man, just figure, Mazda-worshipper, friend of Mazda’s lore, and foe of the D(a)êvas. Born as the son of Pourushaspa, he founds the Mazda-worshipper order and is central to its ritual order, religion, faith, lore, utterances, and law. He abjures the Daêvas’ shelter and headship through questions and consultations with Ahura Mazda, and causes the demon-gods to vanish into the ground. He recites the Ahuna-vairya first, intoning it four times, and asks Ahura Mazda about the primordial word that existed before the created world; he receives its explanation, meaning, structure, and proper performance. He authors the Yasna and speaks a word for it. Zarathustra praises Mazda-made H(a)oma, encounters and questions it, offers it carefully, and seeks blessings and protections. He praises good thoughts, words, and deeds, repudiates their evil counterparts, and declares that he will incite households, villages, Zantus, and provinces to follow the Religion of Ahura in thought, word, and deed. Across the records, his holy Fravashi is repeatedly approached, offered to, propitiated, praised, and worshipped, alongside his sanctity and his religious inheritance.
A worshipper of Mazda and Zarathustra’s order confesses devotion to the Lord’s lore and opposition to the Daêvas.
Settlements, harmed and threatened by enemies, seek H(a)oma’s protection and Zarathustra’s power against violent wicked persons.

Righteousness is a holy ritual, virtue, Lord, lofty lord, and ritual truth. It is the best blessing, associated with weal, and represents ritual order with many holy lords. It receives sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise; encompasses days, festivals, seasons, beings, and observances; and is ascribed to prophets and the invoking saint. It is a seed in Mazda-made offerings, loved by people whose Fravashi receives offerings, and enables Ahura Mazda’s Fravashi to attain its ends.

The Sacrifice is an ongoing ritual of homage, propitiation, praise, and worship. It is offered to Ahura Mazda, the lords of the ritual order, the Yazads, the Bountiful Immortals, and many other holy beings, creations, waters, plants, mountains, festivals, and Fravashis. It begins with offerings and praise, then expands into worship of Mazda-made things and the blessing of good ritual and the Mazdayasnian Faith. Sraosha is invited to be present. The ritual continues with Zaothras and truthfully and scrupulously delivered words, worshipping Ahura Mazda, Zarathustra Spitâma, Righteousness, and holy beings. It proceeds through ritual approaches, praises, offerings, and propitiation.

Zaothra is a ritual offering, closely joined to the Baresman in worship. It is used to approach Ahura Mazda, Mithra, the holy Yazads, and other holy beings with praise, and accompanies the Baresman to its appointed place at Hâvani. As an offering for beneficent or good waters, it has Haoma, fresh milk, and Hadhânaêpata with it. The Zaothras are lifted up and presented with sanctity among the offerings.

Baresman is a ritual plant bundle and ritual object, provided with Zaothra, girdle, binding, sanctity, and wood-billets; it contains stars, moon, and sun. It is approached with worship, praise, prayers, recital, and blessings, then brought with Zaothra to its appointed place at Hâvani and used in approaching holy Yazads. Its binding and spreading are performed with sanctity for propitiation of the Bountiful Immortals. Finally it is spread with punctilious sanctity and presented as an offering with its plant, prayers, recollection, wood-billets, perfume, and other Mazda-made objects.

The Bountiful Immortals are holy, bountiful beings: good, beautiful by name, ever-living, ever-helpful, and associated with holy Fravashis described as brilliant, lofty, devoted, and swift. They rule all aright and dispose of all aright, abiding with the Good Mind of the Lord and of His folk. Across the Yasna records, they are repeatedly approached for propitiation, worship, praise, sacrifice, homage, invocation, dedication, sanctification, and priestly service. Offerings made or presented for them include the Myazda-offering, fresh meat, Baresman with Zaothra, Haoma, milk, Hadhânaêpata, the flesh of the speaker’s body or frame, and the blessings of life or of a prospered life. They are summoned with precept, praise, grace-produced delight, and blessings; they are recipients of the Yasna itself and are sacrificed to with the blessing of the good ritual. Their Fravashis are approached with praise alongside all holy Fravashis of the heavenly Yazads. The records conclude by worshipping them with Ahura Mazda as those who rule and dispose of all aright.

Fire is Ahura Mazda’s son, Mazda-made, sacred, and a holy, lofty lord of the ritual order. It is worshipped as the Yazad of the spoken name and receives sacrifice, homage, propitiation, praise, wood-billets, and perfume. From Yasna III through Yasna XXV, it is repeatedly addressed and worshipped together with all the fires, sacred wood, perfume, and holy waters. Yasna XVII names several fires, Berezi-savangha, Vohu-fryâna, Urvâzista, Vâzista, Spenista, Nairya-sangha, and the fire that is house-lord of all houses. The records consistently present Fire as central to ritual offerings and praise.
Yearly festivals receive offerings for sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise, unfolding through Maidhyô-zaremaya, Maidhyô-shema, Patishahya, Ayâthrima, Maidhyâirya, and Hamaspathmaêdhaya.

l: holy lords of the ritual order, Yasna
s: Holy lords of the ritual order receive praise as the speaker approaches them with Fravashis at appointed times.
Plants are Mazda-made and holy sacred beings, under the holy man’s sovereignty, associated with Zaothras and waters to further teach Mazdayasnians.

l: Zarathustrian law against the Daêvas, Yasna
s: The Zarathustrian law against the Daêvas is Ahura's Faith, a religion praised as most imposing, best, and beautiful; the creed is identified with the Faith of Mazda, and its long descent is worshipped.

Righteousness is pious and good, the lofty lord and ritual essence, named Asha Vahista, the Best. It is a blessing, weal, and the righteous order pervading all things pure, belonging to Ahura Mazda. Zarathustra praises it; worshippers bow to it, dedicate offerings with praise, and seek its enduring protection. It is the basis through which Ahura Mazda knows superior fidelity and sanctity, and it brings weal to one acting rightly toward Best Righteousness. It unfolds through ritual: the Ratu speaks from righteousness; offerings praise it; it is linked to liberality, sovereignty, freedom, glory, and H(a)oma's spring and ritual fountains; finally it provides the best gift associated with the offering.
The holy man utters Blessing and, as holy and sovereign, is to gain absolute will over waters, plants, and sacred creatures, with prayers for freedom and glory.

Ahura Mazda is a resplendent, glorious, holy lord and deity, ruler of this land. He possesses the Kine and Asha, has a house sanctified by H(a)oma, and makes the Kine and holy men. He is chiefly offered and propitiated, makes waters and plants, fathers Fire, appoints rewards and protection, converses with Zarathustra, and indicates religious matters; he is worshipped with the Bountiful Immortals.

l: Day-lords of the ritual order, Yasna
s: Day-lords are holy lords approached in worship, governing the day and receiving offerings; the ritual order unfolds through Hâvani, Sâvanghi, Vîsya, Rapithwina, Uzayêirina, Aiwisrûthrima, and Ushahina.

l: Month-lords of the ritual order, Yasna
s: Month-lords are worshipped ritual-order lords governing months, receiving offerings and praise; they include new, waning, and night-scattering full moons.

advances_to_naming Objects of Propitiation Yasna III advances to the naming of the objects of propitiation. It sets out their approach, praise, sacrifice, homage, and propitiation, and concludes with a priestly exchange between the Zaotar and the Ratu.
Haurvatât is Weal, guarding Mazda-made waters, offered propitiation and requested from Mazda.

Haoma is a sacred, holy plant and complete sacred offering, with a counterpart, Parahaoma, and an associated Haoma-juice. It is Mazda-made, inherently good, righteous, healing, victorious, golden-hued and beautiful; it has bending sprouts, flesh, and branch. It grows widely on mountains, heights, gorges, abysses, snow-peaks, Haraiti, and Peaks-above-the-eagles, in many kinds and forms of milky whiteness or gold. Its healing liquors inspire the pious, and it is called the springs of Righteousness and a source of ritual. Haoma is central to praise and sacrifice. It and its juice are worshipped, offered, propitiated, and approached with punctilious sanctity, including for the Fravashi of Spitâma Zarathustra, Mazda-made waters, and the praise of Ahura Mazda. It accompanies Zaothras, is lifted with sanctity, and is pressed, mixed with milk, poured from a silver cup into a golden chalice, and offered ritually. Zarathustra praises it, its plants, Gâthas, songs, teachings, and health-imparting, victory-giving ritual words. In Yasna IX, H(a)oma comes to Zarathustra as he serves the sacred Fire, calling itself holy and death-driving. It grants inspiration, strength, victory, health, healing, wisdom, prosperity, good husbands for unwed maidens, and other benefits; it lowers Keresâni and is invoked against destroyers of righteousness. In Yasna X its healing, friendship-making, prosperity-giving, and protective power is praised. In Yasna XI it condemns a drinker who withholds its full outpouring, declares itself no head-smiter but far from death, receives an offering, and is credited with binding Frangrasyan in iron. Later it continues to be worshipped with Zaothras, beneficial waters, flesh, and branch.

Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitâma is a holy, saintly Fravashi belonging to Zarathustra Spitâma, identified with him and worshipped as holy. Across the records, it is propitiated with praise or a Yast, receives offerings of Haoma and Haoma-juice, and is finally explicitly worshipped.

l: good waters which Mazda created, Yasna
s: Mazda-created beneficent waters, linked to Zaothra worship, are honored in Yasna XXII through praise to Zaothras and Haoma-water.
Hadhânaêpata is a sacred plant branch praised, lifted up, and offered; it accompanies the Zaothras and Haoma, then is presented to Ahura Mazda and the good waters.

Ratu is a holy, learned, righteous lordship and authority of ritual order, subject to exact regulation and ruling from Righteousness. It creates mental goodness and life’s actions done for Mazda. In the ritual dialogue, Ratu speaks from Righteousness as holy and learned, responds to the Zaotar, commands deserving men to eat the Myazda, and identifies the Zaotar as an Ahû to be revered and chosen. Ratu is itself an Ahû to be chosen.

Holy Yazads are heavenly and earthly beings, holy in spiritual and earthly realms. They receive offerings for propitiation through sacrifice and homage because of Asha Vahista; the speaker approaches them with praise in Zaothra ritual.

l: Mithra, province-lord of the provinces, Yasna
s: has_attributes wide pastures, a thousand ears, and myriad eyes [Yazad of the spoken name] Mithra of the wide pastures receives offerings for sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise. He is described as having a thousand ears and a myriad eyes and as the Yazad of the spoken name.

Mãthra Spenta is a bounteous, holy, effective Zarathustrian law and revelation, instituted and revealed against the Daêvas. It is announced and presented as law and statute, worshipped as glorious and true, identified with the law and its long descent, offered a complete sacred offering, and propitiated in ritual.

The good Mazdayasnian Religion is the faith of the good Religion, of Ahura and according to Zarathustra, with a long descent. Leaders of houses, villages, Zantus, and provinces are urged to follow it through thoughts, words, and deeds. Ancient and spirit-made, it is a star-bespangled girdle borne by Mazda to H(a)oma, who wears it on mountain summits to spread the Mãthra’s precepts and headings and help its teacher. It is worshipped through remembrance, practice, and the Mãthra, maintained in the saint’s understanding.
Myazda is a complete and sacred meat-offering offered with Haurvatât, Ameretatât, and blessed Kine flesh for Sraosha; the Ratu then commands deserving righteous men to eat it.
Wood-billets with perfume are offered to propitiate the Fire and sacrificed to good, pious Prayer for blessings and praise of Ahura Mazda.

Good Yazads are heavenly and earthly beings regarded as fit for sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise. Because of Asha Vahista, or Righteousness the Best, they receive offerings and are approached with sacrifice, homage, and praise throughout the records.

Mazdayasnian is a follower of Zarathustra's order and foe to the Daêvas, devoted to the lore of the Lord and ritual sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise. Mazdayasnians are called to liberality of Righteousness and sacred words; adults are warned against the magician's word. The speaker ultimately confesses this identity.

Zaotar is a priest, Ratu, and speaker in the ritual dialogue. It brings or presides over the Baresman and Zaothra ritual, asks the Ratu to speak forth, and speaks forth as the Ahû to be revered and chosen. Its speech recurs in the concluding exchange and is also associated with a righteous, holy, and learned Ratu.
is_a ritual event The Offering Takes Place through celebrations in which offerings, prayers, recitations, and praises are announced and presented to holy beings.
Good thoughts, foremost for the holy man, are praised and offered to Ahura Mazda and holy beings, while evil thoughts are repudiated.
Good words are offered to Ahura Mazda and holy beings, praised in celebrations, and set against repudiated evil words.
Good deeds, associated with saintly Righteousness, are praised, offered, and presented in celebrations to holy beings, while evil deeds are repudiated.
Haomas are plants offered in celebrations to Ahura Mazda and good waters, accompanying Zaothras and used in Haoma-water.
Haoma-juice, a complete and sacred offering, is offered in praise and for propitiation of Zarathustra Spitâma’s Fravashi.

Prayer for blessings is a timely, good, pious, and beneficent prayer offered with sanctity among sacred sacrifices. In the due course of ritual, it approaches as an offering and is presented as the prayer of the holy lord of ritual order.
present_offerings_to Ahura Mazda [for sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise] Celebrations are used to announce and present offerings to Ahura Mazda and many holy beings.
A sanctified house of Ahura, furthered by offerings with its herds and men, including those born now and those yet to be born.

Ahura Mazda is the Creator, resplendent and glorious, lord of the district and greatest lord and master. Rites seek his propitiation alongside his Fire and creations; worship furthers him, affirms his Kingdom, and asks how serving him includes nourishing the poor.
All Mazda-made holy plants are worshipped as beneficial entities.
Yasna V. is a chapter identified as identical with Yasna XXXVII.
is_identical_with Yasna V. Yasna XXXVII is identified as identical with Yasna V.
A prominent, holy Yast recitation following sacrifice and offering, addressed to the Bountiful Immortals during Yasna, and itself receiving worship.

is_a presentation of offerings [by the priest with the object of propitiation named] Yasna VII presents the priest's complete and sacred offerings, blessings, invocations, and sacrifices to Ahura Mazda, the holy Yazads, sacred beings, and ritual powers.

The Ahuna-vairya is a veracious word, prayer, and sacred gift. Declared before the world’s creation, it contains the seed of righteousness and is worshipped and sacrificed to. Zarathustra first recited it four times, keeping its verses apart and raising his voice. It has five sentences, ending in a concluding fifth sentence, and three stages or measures: good thought, good word, and good deed. Its exact recitation has great stated value; imperfect recitation with additions or omissions has less. It is linked with four classes, five chiefs, and a concluding gift, and is intoned with sanctity, offering saving acts of wisdom and worship.

is_a Mazdayasnians The Zaothras are addressed among the sacred participants in the instruction of Mazdayasnians. They are associated with the waters and plants in causing such people to be further taught.
The wicked are foes rejected by the speaker, to be stripped of power and free choice, repressed, shamed, and hemmed in without power over any wish.
is_a Yasna IX The Hôm Yast concerns H(a)oma, his preparation for the corporeal world by four men, the blessings he grants, and his power against death, enemies, and destructive beings.
Vîvanghvant, first man to prepare H(a)oma for the corporeal world, receives the blessing that Yima will be born to him.

Yima, son of Vîvanghvant, is a brilliant, glorious, sunlike ruler of the corporeal world and many herds. During his reign, herds and people avoid dying, plants and waters avoid drought, food is imperishable, and cold, heat, age, death, and demon-made envy are absent.
Âthwya, the second man to prepare H(a)oma for the corporeal world, receives the blessing of Thraêtaona’s birth.
Heroic tribe member Thraêtaona, born to Âthwya, smote the three-jawed, triple-headed, six-eyed dragon Dahâka.
Dahâka is a three-jawed, triple-headed, six-eyed lie-demon of the Daêvas, endowed with a thousand powers and mighty strength, made by Angra Mainyu to harm settlements and the corporeal world.
A wicked being makes the dragon Dahâka as a mighty destructive force against the corporeal world, settlements, and Asha’s homes.
Thrita, the most helpful of the Sâmas, prepared H(a)oma for the corporeal world and received the blessing of fathering Urvâkhshaya and Keresâspa.
Keresâspa, Thrita’s great, ringlet-headed, bludgeon-bearing son, smote a poisonous dragon that swallowed men and horses, then fled when it sprang from boiling water.
Pourushaspa, fourth preparer of H(a)oma for the corporeal world, receives the blessing of Zarathustra’s birth.
is_a corporeal world The corporeal world is the realm for which H(a)oma was prepared by Vîvanghvant, Âthwya, Thrita, and Pourushaspa. The dragon Dahâka was made as a Drug(k) against it.
is_driven_afar_by H(a)oma Death is driven afar by H(a)oma. Under Yima’s rule there was neither death nor age, and H(a)oma is asked to grant long vitality and the best life of the saints.

The saints are righteous males and females, including holy people, teachers, disciples, children, and those dead, living, unborn, or yet to exist. They possess life, spirit, conscience, and intelligence, strive after ritual righteousness, and may exist within or outside a province. Associated with the best life and radiant heaven, they are protected against those causing their death. Yasna and sacrificial worship are offered to them; worship honors their Fravashis, souls, spirits, consciences, intelligences, and lives, answering all saints with salvation.
Demon-gods, once human-shaped gods flying over earth, were caused by Zarathustra to vanish into the ground.

Sraosha (Obedience) is holy, most beneficent, good, blessed, and Righteous. Dear to the speaker from first to last, it accompanies sacrifice with great glory, is invited to Ahura Mazda’s sacrifice, and receives offerings of sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise.
The cow, a blessed clean creature, curses her driver for selfish fattening despite fair feeding.
A clean, blessed creature with a rider curses one who neglects prayer for swiftness and overdrives racers.
Frangrasyan, a fell Turanian and murderous robber, is bound fast in iron fetters by H(a)oma in this earth’s mid-third.

is_set_apart_for H(a)oma [tongue and left eye as H(a)oma's meal] The offering consists of the tongue and left eye chosen by Ahura for H(a)oma's meal. Anyone who denies, consumes, or withholds it is threatened with household misfortune.
A ritual prayer proclaiming Righteousness as the best blessing and its aid as weal, explained through blessedness and Mãthra, then worshipped, recited, memorised, chanted, and used sacrificially.

is_a confession Yasna XII (Sp. XIII) contains The Mazdayasnian Confession, in which the speaker declares allegiance to Mazda-worship and Zarathustra's order. It records rejection of the Daêvas and praise of Ahura Mazda, Piety, Asha, the Kine, the villages, and the Faith of Mazda.

is_a confession The Mazdayasnian Confession declares the speaker to be a Mazda-worshipper of the order of Zarathustra and estranged from the Daêvas. It praises the well-thought thought, the word well spoken, the deed well done, and the Faith of Mazda.

are_subject_to wasting [through robbery, violence, or drought] The Mazdayasnian villages are protected from robbery, violence against the Kine, drought, wasting, and withering. The speaker declares that he will never become a source of their wasting or withering.
Religious sanctity includes waters, plants, Kine of blessed gift, and Ahura Mazda; the speaker belongs to it, as do Kine and holy men made by Ahura Mazda.
Saoshyant is the holy savior yet to come, the victorious final figure in the sequence from Gaya Maretan.

Prophets are wisest, scrupulous in doctrine and service, devoted to duties, and glorious in thought. Righteousness is ascribed to them; they serve, help, and bless people while labouring to complete the world’s progress and renovation.
The two spirits think, speak, and act the same things; they include Ahura Mazda, the more bountiful Spirit.

l: Fravashi of the Kine of blessed gift, Yasna
s: is_worshipped Kine of blessed gift The Fravashi of the Kine of blessed gift is worshipped.
Gaya Maretan is a holy first created being whose holy Fravashi is worshipped and praised; he begins the succession extending to Saoshyant.
is_a confession and laudation of the Mazdayasnian Faith Hâ fraoreti receives sacrifice as the confession and laudation of the Mazdayasnian Faith.
is_a Yasna Yasna XIV (Sp. XV) contains dedications, offerings, ritual identifications, and dialogue between the Zaotar and the Ratu.

is_a sacrifice [continued with increased fulness of expression] Worship is offered to Ahura Mazda, Zarathustra Spitâma, heavenly and earthly Yazads, the former religions devoted to Righteousness, and various holy creations. It is performed with offered Zaothras and truthfully or faithfully delivered words.
The speaker confesses to belonging to Zarathustra's order.
has_title The Sacrifice Continues Yasna XV (Sp. XVI) is titled The Sacrifice Continues. It presents calls, praises, worship, and invocations connected with the sacrifice.
The Sacrifice Continues concerns the ongoing sacrifice, the worship of the Bountiful Immortals, and the presence of Sraosha (Obedience).

includes the Bountiful Immortals [as its object of acquisition] The creation is described as existing before, emerging into existence, and yet to be, with its actions devoted to Mazda. Ahura Mazda is said to have pronounced the Ahuna-vairya before the creation of the heaven, waters, plants, four-footed cattle, holy man, and the sun.
is_a bounteous word-of-reason Mãthra-spenta, described as the bounteous word-of-reason, is worshipped.
has holy creatures [bountiful and holy] Spirit bounteous is requested from Mazda.

is_a Zand or Commentary [on the Ahuna-Vairya Formulas] Yasna XIX. is a commentary on the Ahuna-vairya and explains its origin, wording, measures, classes, chiefs, spiritual power, and proper recitation. It concludes by offering sacrifice to the Ahuna-vairya and its memorized recital, chanting, and use in the full Yasna.
is_a Zand [commentary] Yasna XX. gives a Zand, or commentary, on the Ashem Vohû and includes a catechetical addition concerning Mazda’s announcements and the Asha Vahista prayer.

l: holy one announced by Mazda, Yasna
s: A holy one announced by Mazda is heavenly and earthly, best, and exercises sovereign power.
A man announced by Mazda is holy and best, ruling without capricious tyranny.

has_title Catechetical Zand Yasna XXI. is presented as a Catechetical Zand concerning the Yênhê Hâtãm. It explains the offering of the Yasna and sacrificial worship and discusses salvation and the best answer given by Mazda.
Commentary on Yênhê Hâtãm explaining Yasna’s addressees and interpreting questions and answers about salvation.

l: holy females headed by Âramaiti, Yasna
s: Holy females headed by Âramaiti receive sacrificial worship as homage to the Bountiful Immortals.
Salvation is a state granted by Ahura as the answer to every saint who exists, is coming into existence, or shall exist.

l: prayers for the approach of the Fravashis, Yasna
s: concern Fravashis [prayers for their approach] They express the speaker’s desire to approach the Fravashis with praise, worship, Yasnas, and homage.

is_a Yasna Yasna XXIV. describes the presentation of ritual offerings, prayers, recollection, and Mazda-made objects to Ahura Mazda, the good waters, divine beings, the Fravashis and souls of the saints, and the Fire of Ahura Mazda.

l: recollection and practice of the good Mazdayasnian Religion, Yasna
s: is_a religious practice [good Mazdayasnian] The recollection and practice of the good Mazdayasnian Religion are presented together with the timely prayer, the heard recital of the Gâthas, and other ritual offerings.
love Righteousness The Fravashi of the people who love Righteousness receives offerings together with all the holy Fravashis of the saints.

This document summarizes Yasna XXVIII–LXXII, a sequence of prayers, teachings, worships, and ritual formulas centered on Ahura Mazda, Zarathustra Spitama, Righteousness (Asha), Good Mind, Piety, the Bountiful Immortals, and the Mazdayasnian Faith. It begins with Zarathustra seeking grace, revelation, understanding, life, and power, while the Soul of the Kine appeals for protection from violence and receives Zarathustra as spiritual master for the diligent tiller. The early units establish the central conflict between the better and worse primeval spirits: Righteousness, truth, and good thoughts, words, and deeds lead toward Ahura Mazda’s Kingdom, Welfare, Immortality, Heaven, and salvation; the Lie, Evil Mind, Daêvas, violence, and false teachers lead to ruin, Hell, and the Lie’s abode. Zarathustra repeatedly asks for divine instruction about creation, righteous rule, protection of people, settlements, cattle, waters, plants, and the poor, while opposing Grehma, the Karpans, Kavis, Bendva, rapacious rulers, and other enemies of the Faith. Named supporters include Kavi Vîstâspa, Frashaostra Hvôgva, and Gâmâspa Hvôgva. The middle portion broadens into worship and sacrifice offered to Ahura Mazda, Fire, the Kine, earth, waters, stars, plants, saints, Haoma, and sacred powers, with confessions, petitions for prosperity and health, and care for the whole clean creation. Later units emphasize the Saoshyant, future saviours, final judgment, the Kinvat Bridge, and the eventual overcoming of evil. Yasna LIII adds marriage counsel for Pourukista and the faithful. The closing sections focus on the Gâthas, Sraosha, ritual worship, mutual blessings, household prosperity, prayers against enemies of holy law, offerings to Fire and waters including Ardvi Sûra Anâhita, and the saving force of correctly recited Yasna words. Yasna LXXII simply directs the reader back to Yasna LXI.
A chapter of prayers seeking grace, revelation, Righteousness, Good Mind, spiritual attainments, long life, and understanding of the primeval world.

Zarathustra is a righteous man, prophet, spiritual master, herald of Ahura Mazda, and chieftain of both the people’s spiritual cause and the rite. He alone among those mentioned has hearkened to the enunciations of Ahura and Asha, and he seeks to declare their doctrines, truths, mighty acts, regulations, and laws to waiting people and living believers. His central commitment is to Righteous Order, Good Mind, Obedience, Ahura Mazda’s will, and the worthy aims of the faith. He rejects disobedience, Evil Mind, arrogance, falsehood, the Lie, and neglect of the Kine, while opposing the wicked and the disciples of the Karpans and Kavis. He begins in prayer, asking Ahura Mazda for spiritual help, long-lasting life, instruction, guidance, protection, and the capacity to teach. He offers his body, thought, word, deeds, Good Mind, Obedience, and Sovereign Power, makes Yasna confessions, and offers propitiation. He seeks Ahura Mazda’s Realm, the good abode, straight paths from Righteous Order, and eternal life in the Realm of Good Mind. As the account unfolds, Zarathustra establishes Ahura Mazda’s precepts, speaks for the faithful, teaches the corporeal world what Ahura Mazda showed him, and guides his voice toward glory through Mãthras and regulations. He is supported by Kavi Vîstâspa and addresses Haêkat-aspas, Frashaostra, and Gâmâspa in advancing the great cause. He is associated with the five holy Gâthas; his words and deeds are worshipped in ritual. In the end, he answers concerning rites and sacrifices, is worshipped with sacrifice as chieftain of the rite and holy lord of ritual order, and receives instruction for prescribed prayers and the last ending of life.

The Bountiful Immortals are good Yazads, male and female givers of good things, who rule and dispose of all aright. They include Ahura Mazda and are the entire body of Ahura Mazda’s holy order; Righteousness the Best is identified as one of them. They are ever living and helpful, dwell beside the pious, guard the Fravashis of saints, and save holy men and saintly women. Across the Yasna, they are worshipped alongside Ahura Mazda and receive sacrifice, homage, propitiation, praise, and the entire collection of the Yasna, Haptanghâiti. Sraosha worships them and sits among them as a companion. They are invoked to rule rightly, dispose of all aright, grant wealth and offspring, and bring salvation through their Righteousness. They seek good Yasnas, praises, sacrifices, homage, and a long continued offering of the entire self.

The Gâthas are sacred, bounteous objects of homage that rule supreme in the holy ritual as leading chants. They receive sacrifice and offerings encompassing riches, persons, bodily and spiritual elements. Worshippers honor them as sources of protection, nourishment, reward, health, progress, growth, sanctity, and gifts. They are the five Gâthas of Zarathustra, whose metres, words, Zand, questions, and answers Sraosha first chanted. The account ends with their holy worship, sacrifice to their hymns, and Ustavaiti intoned as a salvation hail.

Ahura Mazda is a deity: the Great Creator, living Lord, King, Life, Rewarder, Spirit, and sovereign ruler. He is chiefly characterized by beneficence, wisdom, Good Mind, Righteousness, Piety, Sovereign Power, and a bountiful spirit. As creator, he makes the Kine and living creation, Righteousness, waters, plants, earth, stars, sun, moon, clouds, lights, darkness, sleep, and the divisions of time; he gives the waters beneficent names and sustains creation. He establishes and rules a Kingdom of Welfare, guides the faithful, guards both worlds from ruin, and is revealed through Good Mind. He appoints Zarathustra as spiritual master, chieftain, and speaker, hears him, receives his praise and offerings, and is repeatedly petitioned for grace, insight, protection, justice, power, salvation, prosperity, Welfare, Immortality, and long-lasting life. He grants Righteousness, Good Mind, fellowship, sacred reward, righteous helpers, and prosperous eternal life. He supports the righteous and bountiful through Righteous Order and Good Mind, while establishing evil for the evil and holy blessings for the good according to deeds and words. From the first invocations as creator and helper through worship, sacrifice, teachings, judgment, and promised rewards, Ahura Mazda remains the constant source of creation, guidance, moral order, blessing, and final welfare.

Good Mind is a benevolent divine attribute and spiritual, mental power associated with Ahura Mazda and Asha. Implanted by Ahura Mazda within souls and living believers, it is a fatherly presence, a better and quiet mind, and a toiling faculty that supports Ahura Mazda as a fellow-worker. It matters most as the inward source of understanding, truth, righteous thought, worthy words, actions, strength, blessing, spiritual attainment, and advancement of the imperishable Sovereign Kingdom. It establishes and governs that kingdom with Righteous Order, gives life and vigorous might, produces blessed rewards, and blesses pure ones. It stands apart from the oppressor and is opposed by the Daêvas, rival-monarch’s teachings, and those far astray. Across the records, Good Mind is first sought for understanding, the Kingdom, and Zarathustra’s task; it then inspires sacrifices, helps the faithful know truth and serve through wise thoughts, words, and actions, and guides them toward Ahura Mazda. It protects settlements, supports the Kine and the Faith, reveals the best words, actions, wisdom, doctrine, and Mãthra, and enables those carrying out Ahura Mazda’s commandments. Finally, it is truly served, its bright and joyful grace is sought, its institutions are declared, and speakers ask it to approach so their souls may advance in good and attain wished-for recompense.

Righteousness is a divine, holy, moral order: Divine Righteousness, Righteousness the Best, and a Bountiful Immortal endowed with light. Conceived, made, sustained, fathered, and given by Ahura Mazda, it consents with the inspired Word-of-reason and is a sacred inner quality within man as well as a guiding order in settlements and creation. It matters most as the truth and straight path by which believers live, choose, worship, act, receive blessings and the better lot, and establish Ahura Mazda’s precepts. The wise follow it in words and actions; Zarathustra nurtures and seeks it; its supporters further settlements, while evil rulers obstruct it. Beginning as an invoked divine power that grants blessing, gifts, beatitude, glory, and protection from spiritual foulness, it is shown unable to name a suitable guardian for the Kine. It is then chosen by the better spirit, works with Âramaiti, the Good Mind, and the Sovereign Power, and opposes the Demon of the Lie. Throughout, it governs just action, offerings, teaching, rule, protection, worship, marriage, and salvation; strengthens Fire; guards earth; and is established through righteous action, ritual, and beneficence. It abides in the Gâthas, blesses holy people acting through good thoughts, words, and deeds, and concludes by being asked to appear for the village and gain victory over the Demon of the Lie.

Soul of the Kine, soul of the sacred herds and folk, suffers violent assault, desolation, insolence, and thievish might. With no pasture-giver but Ahura and Asha and a powerless lord, it cries for strong-handed help. It is later worshipped with the Kine’s created body and worthy cattle souls.
Obedience is invoked as Ahura Mazda’s greatest assisting guardian, linked with long life, and offered by Zarathustra in deed and speech.
is_a gift [bestowed through Righteousness] Long life is sought from Ahura Mazda. The worshippers ask to win and conquer it through his grace and to receive his help.

Âramaiti is a divine quality, virtue, and personified Piety of the saints, belonging to Ahura Mazda as His attribute and also described as His daughter through good deeds. Approaching with Sovereign Power, the Good Mind, and the Righteous Order, she gives body to the spiritual creations of good and evil and embodies abiding, strenuous endurance. Within the faithful and the worshipper, she is piety, a ready mind, and pious wisdom: she questions the two spirits, seeks understanding of future matters and final states, utters saving regulations, and gives holy blessings through the Good Mind. She supports religious truth, sacred orderliness, just action, righteous beings, good rule, and the Kine’s peace, providing joyful meadows. Bountiful, holy, benevolent, beloved, and sanctifying, she increases Universal Weal, Immortality, and the Righteous Order. Yet she departs from the evil-doer who abandons her through ignorance of Good Mind. Her increase helps instruct seekers, prosper the Kine, and sanctify blessings for offspring.

Kavi Vîstâspa is a heroic Kavi and holy friend for the great cause. Through Piety and the chants of Good Mind, he receives wish and attains wisdom in accordance with Asha. A man of Âramaiti, he offers Ahura Mazda praise and propitiation, makes Yasna confessions, and establishes Sovereign Power, granting it to Maidhyô-mâh the Spitâma.

Frashaostra is holy, blest and foremost within Ahura Mazda’s realm. Given guardian power and headship of the Holy Order, he desires grace, offers propitiation and confessions, and seeks confirmation of his gift. He later asks Zarathustra about memorised rites and completed delivery of the Gâthas.

The world arises to be taught by Ahura Mazda, is made with help through Good Mind, progresses toward perfection, and ends in renovation with destruction falling on the Demon of Falsehood and adherents.

are_offered_to Ahura Mazda [with venerating desire and outstretched hands] The prayers seek gracious help, understanding, spiritual gifts, long-lasting life, protection, and the power to overcome torment. They are offered to Ahura Mazda and the divine qualities, and include requests on behalf of Zarathustra, Vîstâspa, Frashaostra, and the people.

Kine are holy herds: sacred cattle and a pure, joy-creating living creation made by Ahura Mazda. They matter as a source of joy, mental blessings, pleasing homes, lasting strength, peace, and welfare for human life and the land. Their sacred cause is bound to Righteous Order, the waters, plants, Yazads, and the sacred mother-kine. From the beginning, the Kine’s Soul seeks protection from wounding and fearful ravages, along with tillage, pasture, food, comfort, fodder, and a skilled, energetic cattle-chief. Ahura Mazda gives the Kine a path, and she chooses the thrifty husbandman as holy master while rejecting the thieving nomad. Yet evil teachers declare the Kine among the worst things, and wicked men, Grehma, and allies harm or destroy her life. The Kine therefore seek just spiritual leadership, while stint in labour and failure to provide complete pasture are condemned. Their prosperity depends on toil, understanding, merciful care, and the word of the Righteous Order. Worshippers pray to nurture and protect them, providing homes, pastures, and flourishing plants. Ahura Mazda grants joyful meadows of peace, and the Kine remain sought with wealth in herds beside them, supported by waters and plants in the farm-yard.
Spiritual beings unable to choose righteousness, the Demon-gods and worshippers choose the Worst Mind and rush to the Demon of Fury.

Men perform good or evil deeds and are urged to hear, observe, awaken, and choose rightly between two ways. Rival forces deceive them, threatening happy life and Immortality, while wickedness brings long wounding and righteousness brings blessings.

l: the tiller of the earth, Yasna
s: A thrifty, righteous tiller of the earth receives Zarathustra as spiritual master from Ahura and is spared destruction unlike the wicked.
A chieftain is sought as a skilled, energetic guardian to protect the Kine by repelling the wicked’s fury, but none with power and freedom from hate is found.

Mãthra is a word, teaching, incarnate word of reason, and offering of fatness. Declared by the All-wise One as the best and world's first teaching, it proclaims beneficent power, guides the speaker through Righteousness, and is linked to Welfare, Immortality, holiness, and a flourishing Realm. It is declared from Ahura Mazda; disobedience ends in woe, while Sraosha embodies and holds first place in it.
Mãthra, an inspired Word-of-reason opposing the Daêvas, is bounteous and worshipped with its complete, long descent.

The Kingdom, also called a Realm, is good, holy, mighty, and shining with splendour like the sun. It belongs to Ahura Mazda and is associated with good rulers, true saints, and those who follow Righteous Order. Requested from Ahura and Asha for disciples, it begins by giving peaceful home life and quiet happiness against fearful ravages. It is then sought as power to smite the Lie-demon, with headship and vigour given to faithful servants. Worshippers seek it for ever, as Ahura Mazda’s desired holy Realm, through which He gives highest blessings to the right-living poor.
A religious doctrine teaching two opposed primeval spirits, contrasting better and worse thought, word, and deed, and calling hearers to choose rightly and join the great renovation.

Good Mind is a divine, better mind of the Lord: a worshipped presence in the living, within doctrine, and a law for Zarathustra. Invoked with Righteousness, it grounds worshippers’ words and sayings. It empowers believing natures to guard Faith, offers sheltering leadership among folk and commanders, and aids discernment and proclamation of the Faith’s truths, including against Bendva. Within the speaker’s soul it gives grace, understanding, virtue, and guidance, making holy works worthy and radiant. Worshipped with Righteousness and the Gâthas, it ultimately serves as a means by which worshippers may prosper to salvation through divine assistance.

The two first spirits are a pair, independent in action and opposed as better and worse in thought, word, and deed. They differ in thoughts, commands, understandings, beliefs, deeds, consciences, and souls. They come together to determine life, its absence, and the world’s final ordering, after which the more bountiful spirit speaks to the harmful spirit.
A bounteous, better spirit chooses Righteousness and those who content Ahura through faithful actions, clothing itself in heaven’s firm stones.

Evil Spirit chose evil as its realm and works the worst possible results, including the worst life for the wicked. It rules the Daêvas through evil mind and word, seeking to deprive mankind of happy life and Immortality.

The Evil Mind is a personified worst mind, evil disposition, and wickedness expressed through actions. It approaches and is chosen by the Demon-gods, leading them toward Fury and pollution of mortal lives. It is the source of the Daêvas, opposed to the Good Mind, Ahura Mazda, and Righteousness; Zarathustra abjures it, while the wicked remain within it.
A demon allied with Demon-gods, seeking through that alliance to pollute the lives of mortals.

Sovereign Power is a beneficent spiritual power and gift given by Ahura Mazda through holy deeds, words, and sacrifice. It holds priority among Yazads and serves as rule and defense for the faithful. Invoked with Good Mind and Sanctity for salvation, it is sought to grant Zarathustra strength, establish welfare with Righteous Order and Âramaiti, preserve desired wealth, and provide the best rule and defense.

The Demon of the Lie is a powerless demon and drug of the Lie, opposed by Righteousness. It is held captive, delivered to the Righteous Order, defeated, and driven from prophets and the seven Karshvars; at the world’s perfection, it and its adherents are destroyed.

The Daêvas are demon-gods and false religious powers, allied with the Demon of Fury in the great struggle. They are seeds of Evil Mind, ruled by Evil Spirit, linked to the Lie-demon through sacrifice, and cause confusion in human thought. Estranged from Ahura Mazda and Righteousness and forsaken by Good Mind, they are supported by the wicked through evil schemes, words, and perverted Faith and Insight. Their servants possess harmful malice threatening a dwelling and its lord. Yet they are opposed by Mãthra, saints’ good consciences, Sanctity, and Sraosha, who battles and frightens them, destroys them, and hews down the Daêvas of Mazendran.

The righteous are saints who uphold Asha in community and soul and act uprightly with honour. They seek blessings, Weal, and eternal Immortality, receiving salvation and a joyful destiny. After perfection, they gather in the happy abode of the Good Mind and Ahura, while their conscience crushes the wicked at judgment.
